tender.title: Dorset Keyworker Service (BCP Place)
tender.description:
NHS Dorset is seeking a sole Supplier to deliver the Dorset Keyworker Service in the Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole Place area. The KeyWorker Service is a targeted offer that will be provided to children and young people who have been diagnosed with a learning disability and/or who have autism, who are inpatients in, or at risk of being admitted to a mental health hospital to support them and their family in navigating services and reduce the risk of admission to a mental health unit.

The expected service commencement date is 01 February 2027 for an initial term of 14 months with an extension option of 12 months. Value of initial tern £268,333 (£230,000 per annum)

lots.description:
NHS Dorset is seeking a sole Supplier to deliver the Dorset Keyworker Service in the Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole Place area.
The service is for children and young people (CYP) who are:
• Aged 0-25
• Are registered with a Dorset GP or fall under the commissioning responsibility of NHS Dorset
• Live in the BCP Place (Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole Council) area
• Diagnosed with a Learning Disability and/or Autism.
AND
• Rated red or amber as being at risk of hospital admission on the Dynamic Support Register (DSR) OR;
• An inpatient in mental health hospital
• A person in an acute hospital due to a mental health crisis
A population overview is included in Document 4- Specification Requirements Document BCP Keyworker

The service aims will be to:
• Prevent crisis, thus reducing demand on specialist services
• Reduce avoidable in-patient care or use of other restrictive approaches and settings
• Be a consistent point of contact for the individual and their family
• Ensure reasonable adjustments are made by services to enable neurodiverse individuals and those with a learning disability to access the support they require
• Provide signposting, information, and advice
• Advocate for the individual and ensure their voice is heard

The Service will be available across the Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole Council area. The interventions are to be delivered out and about within the communities in which CYP and their families; live, go to school and/or work and will include in their homes.

The expected service commencement date is 01 February 2027 for an initial term of 14 months with an extension option of 12 months. Value of initial tern £268,333 (£230,000 per annum)

tender.title: Specialist Financial Advice Service
tender.description:
Essex County Council (ECC) are committed to investing in a quality financial Information, Advice and Guidance (IAG) offer for our residents that enables the provision of accredited, regulated and specialist as well as maximising the role of communities to deliver preventative support.
Our vision is to deliver high-quality Financial IAG support to Essex residents to improve their financial wellbeing, increase their resilience to withstand future financial shocks, and address the root causes of financial hardship.
The primary scope for the Specialist Financial Advice is predicated on investing in a partner who can provide a strategic, lead provider relationship with ECC:-
•	To maximise the funding and resources aligned to the 'Resilience' and 'Community Connections' strands of the ECC Crisis and Resilience Fund (CRF) programme.  Key to this is being able to monitor and track progress across multiple offers and services and provide impartial advice on future steps.
•	Development of a financial education programme to create more 'financial confidence' in Essex.  Education is central to prevention. It builds confidence and capability to make informed decisions, recognise problems early, and seek help before crisis. By equipping individuals with financial literacy skills to help with things like budgeting and saving, we can reduce demand for high-cost, specialist interventions.
•	System Development - Community partners play a key role in prevention, early intervention, and post-advice support. They have trusted relationships with residents and can spot early signs of financial stress, can act as first-contact navigators and referrers, and provide ongoing wraparound support. Building this capacity can allow Accredited, Regulated & Specialist providers to focus their resources on more complex needs.
 The partner is required to:-
•	Act as a source of 'warm referrals' from the CRF crisis payment scheme, tracking cases over providers to ensure household get the advice they need, and can achieve the results they need to lessen and avoid future crisis.
•	Advice must be appropriately accredited - i.e. regulated financial activity should be authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), unless appropriate exemptions or exclusions are in place.
•	The service must offer multiple access routes (online, in-person, telephone) with clear signposting to referral points; ensures inclusion for digitally excluded and those needing face-to-face support.
•	The intention is to procure this via an outcomes-based specification, with space for evolution of the activities in collaboration with the successful bidder.
•	The delivery approach for all services under this contract must be person-centred, needs-based, trauma-informed.
The outcomes expected from the contract are:-
•	Increased savings,
•	Reduced priority debt, reduced need for emergency food parcels,
•	Reduced material deprivation,
•	Maximised income,
•	Fewer repeat crisis applications,
•	Increased access to appropriate and quality advice services.
The expected deliverables are:-
•	Accessible referrals routes and triage methods so residents can be moved seamlessly between IAG support and wraparound services (such as affordable food, skills and employment, Housing etc.).  
•	Standardised referral and triage frameworks with clear escalation pathways - helps to foster "no wrong door" approach to ensure residents receive holistic support regardless of entry point into system.
•	A single case management tool which can be used by all partners is not essential but a significant advantage.
•	Ensure consistent quality Financial IAG standards across the county (no postcode lotteries).  Assurance will be from not only your submissions, but feedback from households engaged in the services and other service providers.
•	Self-serve digital/website options provided for those that can and want to access - i.e. benefits calculators, resources, signposting to national helplines - provides clear, jargon-free, and trusted financial Information advice and guidance.
•	Practical tools such as budget planners, debt management guides, and benefit eligibility checkers.
•	The above resources also available in non-digital formats.
•	Data-led approach to target support to vulnerable households.  Being able to collect ,store and displays such information in a GDPR compliant manner.
•	Work with system partners to engage and support with priority cohorts. You will be lead provider bringing together the necessary expertise from across the system to deliver the outcomes.
•	Provide outreach support to community locations such as libraries, food banks, community supermarkets, community hubs.
•	Accessible learning formats such as online modules, community workshops, and integrated modules with other educational actors in the sector, such as (but not limited to) ECC adult community learning and ECC Libraries.
•	Cohort-specific content such as options for young people, families and those transitioning through life events (i.e. retirement, job losses or armed forces personnel leaving service).
•	Foundational training for community staff and volunteers on basic financial literacy, benefits awareness, and signposting to create 'Money Advice Champions' embedded in community settings.
•	Developing a countywide knowledge hub with best practice guides, templates, and data insights to support community partners.
•	 A "Community Advice Partner" recognition scheme to ensure light-touch quality assurance of IAG in community settings.
Prospective bidders are advised that the Council will finalise the scope of the forthcoming procurement opportunity following the conclusion of the market engagement stage and reserves the right to amend the scope of this service accordingly.
For the avoidance of any further doubt, please be advised that any dates for the proposed procurement opportunity are provided for indicative purposes only and the Council reserves the right to amend this information following confirmation of the procurement timetable for this project. Full details of the structure of this procurement and associated timetable will be detailed within the corresponding Contract Notice in due course.

tender.title: Communal Recycling Innovation Challenge 2026
tender.description:
West London Waste Authority is seeking interested suppliers for early market engagement for Communal Recycling Innovation.
Communal Recycling Innovation Challenge 2026
Can your organisation help transform recycling in communal housing?
West London Waste Authority (WLWA), working in partnership with its six constituent boroughs (Brent, Harrow, Hillingdon, Hounslow, Ealing and Richmond), is seeking innovative solutions to improve the capture and segregation of recycling and food waste in communal properties.
Recycling performance in communal properties consistently lags behind kerbside collections. Improving participation, reducing contamination and increasing food waste capture remains one of the sector's greatest challenges.
We recognise that there is no single solution to this challenge. We are therefore inviting organisations from across the public and private sectors to bring forward fresh innovative ideas that could make a measurable difference.
We welcome proposals from organisations including:
•	Waste and recycling companies
•	Technology and AI providers
•	Behavioural science and communications specialists
•	Housing and property technology providers
•	Universities and research organisations
•	Start-ups, SMEs and social enterprises
The Challenge
We are looking for innovative solutions that can help deliver one or more of the following outcomes:
•	Increase recycling capture from communal properties
•	Increase food waste participation
•	Reduce contamination of recycling
•	Improve resident engagement and behaviour change
•	Generate better operational insight through data and technology
•	Deliver scalable, cost-effective solutions that could be replicated across London and beyond.
Solutions may involve technology, infrastructure, resident engagement, digital platforms, operational improvements, behavioural interventions or other innovative approaches.
This initiative will be delivered in two stages.
Stage 1 - Expression of Interest - closing date 22/09/26
Organisations are invited to submit a short overview of their proposed solution, including:
•	The challenge being addressed
•	A summary of the proposed innovation
•	Evidence of effectiveness (where available)
•	The potential benefits and scalability of the solution
Stage 2 - Shortlisting and Innovation Pitch - Estimated 20/10/26
Shortlisted organisations will receive a detailed briefing pack, including background information, supporting evidence and project requirements. They will then be invited to submit a more detailed proposal and present their solution to a Communal Recycling Innovation Evaluation panel. This collaborative process is intended to identify the most promising ideas for potential pilot projects and future implementation across West London.
Interested? Help us solve one of the UK's biggest recycling challenges
If your organisation has an innovative solution that could improve recycling performance in communal housing, we would like to hear from you.
For informal discussions please contact: Alistair Green - Head of Municipal Waste Development: 
alistairgreen@westlondonwaste.gov.uk

tender.description: NHS Devon sought to procure a managed Pathway 1 home-based intermediate care support service for Plymouth - to fully manage provision to support circa 60-80 individuals at any one time on our Intermediate Care pathway in the community following a period of acute/medical intervention.

lots.description:
This notice is an intention to award a contract under the most suitable provider process.
NHS Devon has a requirement for a fully CQC compliant service, with a minimum rating of good, to fully manage provision to support circa 60-80 individuals at any one time on our Intermediate Care pathway in the community following a period of acute/medical intervention. This service will be on a block basis through a set number of hours of delivery and reimbursed at a fixed hourly rate to encompass all costs. Due to operational demand, this service provision will need to remain flexible in response to system needs and may therefore need to be increased against the 60-80 baseline.
The service is designed to support people following:
• Acute hospital stay (step down)
• A bedded Intermediate Care pathway (step-down)
• Deterioration in the community to prevent hospital admission (step up)
Intermediate Care Pathway 1 personal care, rehab and reablement, will be short-term, time-restricted, supporting a goal-based period of care that calls on a mixture of health and social care assessments and interventions to support people to maximise their potential to live as independently as possible by recovering or continuing to improve skills because of those interventions.
The service will operate on a 7-day basis (including bank holidays) between the core operating hours of 7am and 11pm and accepting referrals during this time. The service operates 24/7 'on call' and 'out of hours' cover.
This service will include but is not limited to: people living with frailty, mild cognitive impairment, dementia or delirium, palliative and end of life care needs, mental health conditions, learning disabilities, autism, obesity (including bariatric patients), younger adults, and people living in an unsafe environment, experiencing homelessness, or at risk of homelessness.
Further information was included in the PIN previously published for this procurement.
The exact pricing arrangements are subject to contract negotiation but the approximate maximum lifetime value including extension is £4.5m
Although elements of this service are existing, as a fully managed service it is a new requirement.
The intended supplier holds other contracts but is new to provision of these arrangements. 
The Contract length will be an initial 18 months with an extension option of up to 12 months. Target start date is 01/10/2026 but this may be subject to ammendment.

tender.title: Let's Talk Money - Debt and Housing Support Services
tender.description:
The service is jointly funded through the Housing Support Grant (HSG) and the Children’s and Communities Grant (CCG – Families First) and is designed to support individuals and families experiencing financial instability where debt is a primary driver of housing risk, homelessness, or wider family instability.  
The aim of the service is to prevent homelessness, sustain tenancies, and improve family resilience through hands‑on, needs‑led and practical support delivered via a single lead worker model. This includes financial capability and budgeting support, managing debt by securing viable debt solution options, and addressing housing‑related issues that may impact financial stability or tenancy sustainment.
The service is referral‑led, accessed primarily through the Housing Support Gateway, and is specifically designed for individuals and families who do not engage well with appointment‑based or advice‑only services. This includes people who are homeless, living in temporary accommodation, sofa surfing, or experiencing complex needs.
The service does not deliver general welfare benefits advice, mandatory reconsiderations or appeals. These functions are delivered through existing commissioned services. An exception applies to Child Disability Living Allowance (DLA), which may be supported under the Families First element of the service only.
While the service promotes independence, the Provider must deliver supported actions where vulnerability, complexity or executive‑function barriers prevent individuals from completing tasks independently.
The service must take a proactive and preventative approach, supporting individuals to build long‑term financial resilience, reduce debt, prevent homelessness and sustain tenancies. Housing instability and financial instability are often interconnected; therefore, the service must address both areas holistically.
Full service requirements will be defined and issued in the tender pack following supplier engagement.

tender.description:
The London Academy of Excellence (LAE) is a sixth form for scholars of all backgrounds, cultures and experiences. LAE consistently delivers outstanding A level results for all students but has achieved particular success helping students from less-advantaged backgrounds win places at the best universities in the UK and around the world. The Academy mission is to promote social mobility for students from backgrounds considered disadvantaged. 
LAE is one of the highest-performing academic sixth forms in the United Kingdom. Our students have a strong sense of pride in belonging in the diverse, inclusive and friendly LAE community centred on London’s dynamic East End. 
LAE is moving to a brand-new premises in July of 2026 (early occupancy) and will welcome its students back to the new building in September 2026. This is an exciting opportunity for the right cleaning provider to partner with LAE in keeping their standards high in all areas, including cleaning. The premises is an impressive and modern building which has been resourced with robust and resilient furnishings to withstand the education environment. The building is stretched across 8 floors with bright open spaces to compliment the Academy.
Further information regarding the Academy can be obtained here: https://www.lae.ac.uk/
Tender information:
The successful tenderer will be required to provide excellent cleaning services at LAE, which has 625 pupils and 80 teaching and support staff which will increase to 750 pupils and 90 teaching and support staff by September 2027.  
The contract term being tendered for 3 years, from 01/09/2026 – 31/08/2029. There is an option for a further extension period for up to two additional years to 31/08/2031. 
The contract offers an excellent opportunity to review and propose enhancements to the current cleaning services, for the new building. The contract includes both core term time cleaning and periodic deep cleaning throughout the year.
The school is keen to secure a high quality cleaning service whereby its students are able to enjoy excellence in education, supported by excellently kept facilities. 
The Academy expects both a tightly managed service and high levels of productivity to be delivered by the cleaning staff at all times, and expects a management style delivered by the successful contractor that supports, encourages and develops the cleaning staff who are proud to contribute to LAE life. 
The Academy is not obliged to accept the lowest price submitted for this tender, rather the Academy is keen to secure best value from this contract and to deliver best value to its students. Innovative and creative ideas as to how the cleaning services can be developed and improved, will be welcomed. The Academy seeks a contractor that is keen to work in partnership and who will deliver to its highest abilities, at all times. 
Competitive Flexible Procedure 
This procurement will be run under the Competitive Flexible Procedure. This will follow a two stage approach, with stage 1 being the Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ). Here a minimum of 5 candidates (or less, in the event less than 5 meet the minimum criteria) and a maximum of 10 candidates, will progress to stage 2. Any selection of tenderers will be based solely on the criteria set out for the procurement and a minimum score of 60% must be achieved. 
Selected tenderers will then be invited to stage 2, the Invitation To Tender (ITT). Here, the evaluation of tender response will be set as 35% price and 65% quality.
Value of contract:
The annual value of the current contract is £62,000 however the new building will be almost twice the size so the estimated value is circa £124,000
Therefore the value of this contract is £620,000 
The contract shall be a fixed price contract with invoices raised monthly to the Academy. 
Additional requirements and information:
•The Academy has a minimum requirement for a contractor’s employers' liability and public liability insurances of £5 million 
•The minimum annual turnover that your company must have achieved to be considered for this opportunity is £500,000
•The client aspires to move towards London living wage
•There are not any incumbent cleaning staff currently within the Local Government Pension Scheme  
•The cleaning services are currently contracted to Birkin Group  
•Please note that the successful tenderer will be required to pay the RIVA tender fee for this project directly to RIVA, upon their contract award.
•The client reserves the right not to appoint in conclusion of this project.

Universal Sleep Support Model (Bradford District and Craven)

The service provides training and material for the children and young people workforce and specialist one-to-one sleep clinics for parents of children, aged 2-11 years old who are experiencing sleep difficulties. Sleep practitioners work with families to create a personalised sleep plan for their child.

The service aims to provide a flexible tiered support for families in partnership with family hubs to promote good sleep habits and reduce the need for specialist support by intervening early.

The service supports the development of a sleep pathway for Bradford District & Craven and is delivered in line with NICE clinical guidance and guidelines:
CG170 Autism Spectrum Disorder in Under 19s: Support and management
NG87 Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: diagnosis and management.

tender.title: Danby Lodge overflow car park construction and groundworks
tender.description:
The North York Moors National Park Authority has undertaken a number of significant improvements at Danby Lodge in recent years as part of a wider strategy to enhance the site as a flagship visitor destination and support the Authority's second statutory purpose of promoting opportunities for the understanding and enjoyment of the National Park.
To support these improvements and accommodate increasing visitor demand, the Authority is seeking to improve the existing overflow car park through the installation of a reinforced hardstanding surface capable of year-round use.
The proposal will provide approximately 60 parking spaces within the footprint of the existing overflow parking area, which has been used for many years during periods of high visitor demand and to support events hosted at Danby Lodge.
The development will utilise a permeable cellular reinforcement system with a stone-filled finish, creating a durable, weather-resistant surface whilst retaining a natural appearance appropriate to its National Park setting. The design has been developed to minimise visual impact and protect surrounding environmental interests.
Surface water will continue to be managed through the existing drainage infrastructure, with runoff directed into the French drain network installed as part of previous site improvement works. The permeable nature of the proposed surfacing will assist with drainage and reduce ground disturbance associated with the current grassed surface.
The proposed works have also been designed to avoid any impact on the existing ground source heating infrastructure located beneath the site. The reinforced surface will be constructed above the buried ground source pipe network, ensuring the continued operation and protection of this renewable energy system.
The successful contractor will be expecting to work closely with our woodland and ecology Officers to ensure that approved plan is carried out as approved

tender.title: Ecohydrological survey and hydrological restoration plan at Roudsea Wood and Mosses NNR - 2026/2027
tender.description:
This study is funded by and contributes toward the Species Recovery Programme - Raised Bog Lagg Restoration Boosting Species Recovery project. The four species that project addresses are:
-	Carex flava - Large Yellow Sedge (a vascular plant)
-	Coenophila subrosea - Rosy Marsh Moth
-	Rheumaptera hastata - Argent and Sable Moth
-	Hagenella clathrata - Window-winged Sedge (a caddisfly)
This contract spans two financial years 2026/27 and 2027/28 to enable background research and a full field season to take place.
The aims of this project are to
-understand and characterise the development of the peatlands at Roudsea and the likely pre-modification status of habitats and ecohydrology.
- understand how modifications from this 'reference' state have influenced the development of what we see today, and how this can be remediated.
- understand how the status of the four species is likely to have been affected by these changes.
- identify where and how these habitats are hydrologically damaged.
- to model the impacts of sea level rise on these habitats and species.
- to design a restoration plan to restore (within the project area) the hydrology of the SSSI Lowland Raised bog, the fen habitat within the wood and to maximise opportunities for the habitats and the four protected species to thrive and be resilient to the impacts of climate change and sea level rise.
